# NYC Motor Vehicle Collisions — Crashes

Source: NYC Open Data, dataset `h9gi-nx95` ("Motor Vehicle Collisions - Crashes"), published by the NYPD. Snapshot downloaded 2026-10-03.

Official description (paraphrased): each row is one police-reported motor vehicle collision in New York City. A police report (MV-104AN) is required when someone is injured or killed, or when there is at least $1,000 of damage. The data is preliminary and subject to change.

File: `crashes.parquet` (one row per crash)

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| collision_id | BIGINT | Unique identifier of the crash |
| crash_date | DATE | Date of the crash |
| crash_time | TIME | Time of the crash |
| borough | VARCHAR | Borough where the crash occurred |
| zip_code | VARCHAR | Postal code of the crash location |
| latitude, longitude | DOUBLE | Coordinates of the crash location |
| location | VARCHAR | Latitude/longitude pair |
| on_street_name | VARCHAR | Street on which the crash occurred |
| cross_street_name | VARCHAR | Nearest cross street |
| off_street_name | VARCHAR | Street address if known |

# NYC Motor Vehicle Collisions — Crashes

Source: NYC Open Data, dataset `h9gi-nx95` ("Motor Vehicle Collisions - Crashes"), published by the NYPD. Snapshot downloaded 2026-10-03.

Official description (paraphrased): each row is one police-reported motor vehicle collision in New York City. A police report (MV-104AN) is required when someone is injured or killed, or when there is at least $1,000 of damage. The data is preliminary and subject to change.

File: `crashes.parquet` (one row per crash)

| Column | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| collision_id | BIGINT | Unique identifier of the crash |
| crash_date | DATE | Date of the crash |
| crash_time | TIME | Time of the crash |
| borough | VARCHAR | Borough where the crash occurred |
| zip_code | VARCHAR | Postal code of the crash location |
| latitude, longitude | DOUBLE | Coordinates of the crash location |
| location | VARCHAR | Latitude/longitude pair |
| on_street_name | VARCHAR | Street on which the crash occurred |
| cross_street_name | VARCHAR | Nearest cross street |
| off_street_name | VARCHAR | Street address if known |
| number_of_persons_injured / _killed | INTEGER | People injured / killed |
| number_of_pedestrians_injured / _killed | INTEGER | Pedestrians injured / killed |
| number_of_cyclist_injured / _killed | INTEGER | Cyclists injured / killed |
| number_of_motorist_injured / _killed | INTEGER | Vehicle occupants injured / killed |
| contributing_factor_vehicle_1 … _5 | VARCHAR | Factor contributing to the crash, for each vehicle involved |
| vehicle_type_code1 … 5 | VARCHAR | Type of each vehicle involved |

python3 << 'EOF'
import duckdb, pandas as pd
import matplotlib
matplotlib.use("Agg")
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt

con = duckdb.connect()
df = con.sql("""
SELECT CAST(strftime(crash_date,'%Y') AS INT) AS year,
       SUM(number_of_persons_killed) AS killed
FROM 'data/crashes.parquet'
WHERE strftime(crash_date,'%Y') BETWEEN '2016' AND '2025'
GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
""").df()
print(df)

df["killed"] = df["killed"].astype(int)

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(10, 6))
bars = ax.bar(df["year"], df["killed"], color="#c0392b", width=0.65, zorder=3)
ax.plot(df["year"], df["killed"], color="#2c3e50", marker="o", linewidth=2, zorder=4)

for b, v in zip(bars, df["killed"]):
    ax.text(b.get_x() + b.get_width()/2, v + 4, str(v), ha="center", va="bottom",
            fontsize=11, fontweight="bold", color="#2c3e50")

ax.set_title("NYC Motor Vehicle Crash Deaths by Year, 2016–2025", fontsize=15, fontweight="bold", pad=14)
ax.set_xlabel("Year")
ax.set_ylabel("People killed")
ax.set_xticks(df["year"])
ax.set_ylim(0, df["killed"].max() * 1.18)
ax.grid(axis="y", linestyle="--", alpha=0.4, zorder=0)
ax.spines[["top", "right"]].set_visible(False)

avg = df["killed"].mean()
ax.axhline(avg, color="#7f8c8d", linestyle=":", linewidth=1.6, zorder=2)
ax.text(df["year"].iloc[-1] + 0.1, avg, f" 10-yr avg: {avg:.0f}", va="center",
        fontsize=9, color="#7f8c8d")

fig.tight_layout()
fig.savefig("out/nyc_traffic_fatalities_2016_2025.png", dpi=150)
print("saved")
EOF

part.text:
## People killed in NYC motor vehicle crashes, 2016–2025

| Year | People killed |
|---|---:|
| 2016 | 246 |
| 2017 | 256 |
| 2018 | 231 |
| 2019 | 244 |
| 2020 | 269 |
| 2021 | **297** (peak) |
| 2022 | 290 |
| 2023 | 280 |
| 2024 | 268 |
| 2025 | **229** (low) |
| **Total** | **2,610** (avg 261/yr) |

Chart saved to `out/nyc_traffic_fatalities_2016_2025.png`.

**Trend:** Fatalities were flat in the mid-240s through 2019, jumped during the pandemic years (269 in 2020, peaking at 297 in 2021), then fell four straight years to 229 in 2025 — a 23% drop from the peak and the lowest annual total of the decade (2 below the prior low of 231 in 2018).

**Notes:** Sum of `number_of_persons_killed` per crash year; only 36 records in 2016–2025 have a null value (treated as 0), so the totals are unaffected. Per the README, the NYPD data is preliminary and subject to revision.
